title: Quantum capacity of the qubit depolarizing channel
formal: Determine \(Q(q)\), the unassisted asymptotic quantum capacity of \(D_{q}(\rho )=(1- q)\rho +(q/3)(X\rho X+Y\rho Y+Z\rho Z)\), for every real \(q\in [0,1]\). Capacity is measured in reliably transmitted qubits per independent channel use, under the coding definition below.
definitions: \(\rho\) is a one-qubit density matrix. The Pauli operators satisfy \(X|0\rangle =|1\rangle , X|1\rangle =|0\rangle , Z|0\rangle =|0\rangle , Z|1\rangle =- |1\rangle\) and Y=iXZ. Thus q is the total probability of a nonidentity Pauli error, each type having probability \(q/3\). For block length n, choose an integer \(k_{n}\ge 0\) and completely positive trace-preserving maps \(E_{n}\) from \(k_{n}\) qubits to n qubits and \(R_{n}\) from n qubits to \(k_{n}\) qubits. Let |\(\Phi _{k}\rangle =2^{- k/2}\sum_{x\in \{0,1\}^{k}}|x\rangle _{A}|x\rangle _{B}\), and define \(F_{n}=\langle \Phi _{k_{n}}|[id_{A}\otimes (R_{n}\circ D_{q}^{\otimes n}\circ E_{n})](|\Phi _{k_{n}}\rangle \langle \Phi _{k_{n}}|)|\Phi _{k_{n}}\rangle\). A rate \(r\ge 0\) is achievable if there is a sequence of such codes with \(\liminf _{n} k_{n}/n\ge r\) and \(F_{n}\to 1\). \(Q(q)\) is the supremum of achievable rates. Sender and receiver have no initially shared entanglement, classical side channel, feedback, or auxiliary quantum channel. Encoding and recovery may be computationally unrestricted and jointly process an entire block. The same q is used independently on every channel use. This definition concerns transmission of quantum states, not merely classical bits through a quantum device.
answer_criterion: Supply an unambiguous real-valued function g on all real \(q\in [0,1]\), and prove in Lean that |\(g- Q(q)|\le 1/100\) pointwise throughout that domain, in the units stated in the definitions. The answer must establish lower and upper bounds with this uniform error guarantee. An exact determination also qualifies. A finite set of sample values, an uncertified plot, or a restatement of the defining optimization or limit does not determine the curve. No predetermined formula grammar or polynomial evaluation-time requirement is imposed. This numerical acceptance criterion does not assert exact equality with a conjectured curve.
why: The unresolved communication limit of a canonical quantum-noise model. It tests whether quantum coding theory can turn regularized existence formulas into sharp quantitative limits despite degeneracy and multi-copy advantages.

importance.reason: A benchmark capacity problem connecting quantum error correction, information-theoretic converses and the operational effect of entangled encodings.

progress.text: Cerf derives no-cloning upper bounds for Pauli channels, including the depolarizing zero-capacity boundary.
Devetak proves quantum coding and converse results underlying the regularized coherent-information formula.
Leditzky–Leung–Smith determine low-noise capacities to leading orders; their arXiv v3 strengthens a lemma in December 2023.
Zhu and coauthors revise geometric optimization bounds; this work is presented at TQC on 4 September 2026.
Agarwal and coauthors revise improved capacity-threshold lower bounds from symmetric rank-two states.
Kondra and coauthors give exponential strong converses for degradable and antidegradable channels.
Krohn-Grimberghe’s v2 retains certified positivity at total Pauli error \(q=0.194868\) and clarifies the scope of the certificate claims.

status_note: Exact unassisted capacity remains open in the 2026 primary literature. The August certificate improves a positive-capacity lower bound, without claiming an exact threshold or capacity formula. All displayed thresholds use total Pauli error q. Review cutoff: 11 September 2026. The 12 September 2026 edit adopts absolute 0.01 benchmark acceptance; the saved open-status evidence concerns the underlying exact question and does not independently certify openness at that tolerance.

context_blocks.text: This channel is a basic model of unbiased qubit noise: a bit flip, a phase flip, or both occur with equal probabilities. Its one-parameter definition hides a hard coding problem. A quantum code must preserve superpositions and correlations with a reference system, which is why the fidelity test in the definition uses half of a maximally entangled state. Correctly transmitting only computational-basis strings would test a weaker, classical task.

Noise conventions differ substantially between papers. In this card q is the total Pauli error probability. A paper writing probabilities \((1- 3p,p,p,p)\) uses \(p=q/3\). A paper writing \((1- \lambda )\rho +\lambda I/2\) uses \(\lambda =4q/3\) on the usual mixture range \(q\le 3/4\). For example, \(q=3/4\) completely erases the input, even though the channel formula remains a valid quantum channel for all \(q\le 1\). The 2026 threshold values below have been converted to q once.

Quantum coding theorems give an exact but unbounded optimization: \(Q(q)=\sup _{n} \max _{\sigma} I_{c}(\sigma ,D_{q}^{\otimes n})/n\). Here \(I_{c}\) is the output entropy minus the entropy jointly held by the output and a purifying reference, with entropy \(S(\tau )=- Tr(\tau  \log _{2}\tau )\). This regularization permits inputs entangled across channel uses. It identifies the mathematical quantity, but does not by itself evaluate this particular function.

Using a maximally mixed one-qubit input gives the hashing lower bound \(\max \{0,1- h_{2}(q)- q \log _{2}3\}\), where \(h_{2}\) is binary entropy and \(0 \log _{2}0\) is interpreted as zero. The expression becomes zero near \(q=0.1893\). Degenerate quantum codes can surpass this benchmark because multiple physical errors can have the same effect on the encoded information. Consequently counting error types as if each required separate correction can underestimate achievable rates.

Agarwal and coauthors’ May 2026 paper searches rank-two input states inside the permutation-symmetric subspace, using representation theory to evaluate many-copy coherent information. It reports a 45-copy numerical positivity threshold \(p=0.064657\), or \(q=0.193971\) here, and explains how degeneracy suppresses the effective environment entropy. This is evidence for better codes and a lower bound on the true threshold, not an optimization over all possible block lengths and states.

Krohn-Grimberghe’s August revision provides an explicit 45-copy state with exact-arithmetic certificates for positive coherent information at \(q=48717/250000=0.194868\). The result extends positivity to smaller q by channel composition and data processing. The preprint distinguishes the threshold printed in the May paper from a stronger state in its authors’ public repository, and bounds both that state and the new witness using certified arithmetic. The certificates are supplied by the author; this review checked the stated bounds and conventions but did not independently rerun the verification artifact.

On the upper-bound side, \(Q(0)=1\) and \(Q(q)=0\) for every \(q\ge 1/4\). In the latter range the channel is antidegradable: the environment can simulate the receiver’s output. Reliable positive-rate transmission would then permit incompatible copies of unknown quantum information. Between the current positive-capacity lower bound and \(q=1/4\), even the location where capacity vanishes remains unsettled. Determining that location would still leave the positive-rate curve to be determined with the required accuracy.

There are also finer results away from the threshold. Leditzky, Leung and Smith control the gap between single-letter coherent information and capacity at low noise through approximate degradability. Zhu and coauthors optimize channel extensions to obtain tighter upper bounds, with their work presented at TQC 2026. These techniques reduce the gap without proving that a proposed family of codes is optimal at every noise value.

Kondra and coauthors’ August 2026 strong-converse result concerns fidelity decay above capacity for degradable and antidegradable channels. Such a theorem strengthens the operational meaning of an upper bound, but does not supply the unknown capacity curve of the depolarizing channel in its intermediate regime. A full resolution here must match the best achievable rates with upper bounds that apply to arbitrary encodings and arbitrary block lengths.

sentences: A depolarizing channel models a qubit subjected to randomly chosen Pauli errors.
Its quantum capacity measures how much unknown quantum information can be transmitted reliably per channel use when many uses are encoded together.
The goal is the capacity curve throughout the noise range under the unassisted coding convention fixed in the card.
Coding across several uses can behave differently from optimizing a single use, which complicates attempts to match achievable rates with impossibility bounds.
The Lean benchmark accepts a certified determination with absolute error at most 0.01 throughout the stated numerical domain.
